A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniversalRAG study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, routing and granularity analyses, retrieval latency measurements, and out-of-domain results in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds embedding visualizations for Qwen3-VL-Embedding in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The modality- and granularity-aware retrieval procedure, trained and training-free routers, losses, routing thresholds, and ensemble strategies are unchanged. Qwen3-VL-Embedding is not introduced into the proposed pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten in-domain and six out-of-domain datasets, with the same query modalities, retrieval corpora, and task requirements. Appendix E's additional encoder does not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retrieval and generation evaluations is unchanged. Qwen3-VL-Embedding appears only in Appendix E's embedding-space diagnostic, without a reported comparison against UniversalRAG.

E3.justification: The reported splits, metrics, training budgets, frame sampling, and benchmark evaluation procedures are unchanged. The additional encoder visualization uses the existing t-SNE/PCA diagnostic without a reported protocol revision.

E4.justification: Appendix E extends the modality-gap analysis from five encoders to six by adding t-SNE and PCA visualizations for Qwen3-VL-Embedding. The existing ablations, robustness analyses, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A.3 retains the statement that results come from a single run because of limited computational resources. Neither version adds repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figure 7 newly reports modality-separated embedding clusters for Qwen3-VL-Embedding. Existing numerical benchmark results, earlier plotted results, and case-study outcomes are unchanged.

T1.justification: Propositions 1–3, their assumptions, equations, and proofs remain unchanged. Appendix C contains grammatical and cross-reference edits without revised mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: v4 adds the descriptor 'any-to-any,' but retains the same described scope of routing across heterogeneous corpora. The central claims about modality gaps, granularity, benchmark superiority, efficiency, and generalization are unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of routing, context sufficiency, generalization, and failure conditions are retained, as are the limitations concerning noisy routing labels and granularity supervision. Appendix E extends supporting evidence without changing its mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain the same, including visual/text similarity weighting, 32-frame sampling, router hyperparameters, hardware, and appendix prompts. The project access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Liang et al. (2022) on modality gaps and Li et al. (2026) on Qwen3-VL-Embedding, and replaces the Riedler and Langer citation with Shalev-Arkushin et al.'s ImageRAG. Other reference changes largely update metadata for retained works.

P1.justification: v4 makes scattered wording and cross-reference edits, introduces 'any-to-any' terminology, updates author details, adds acknowledgements, and edits bibliography metadata. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 7 expands from a two-by-five to a two-by-six panel arrangement, adding Qwen3-VL-Embedding and reducing existing panel sizes. Other figures and tables are retained, with limited text and pagination reflow.

improvement.justification: The added Qwen3-VL-Embedding visualizations modestly strengthen the modality-gap motivation by showing that separation persists in another encoder. Citing Liang et al. (2022) also improves attribution of that motivation. The central benchmark evidence, method, proofs, and single-run reporting remain unchanged, making the overall improvement limited.
